title: Everyone's own AI made the group worse
hook: EVERYONE GOT THEIR OWN AI AND IT BACKFIRED

lines: Okay, picture this. Everyone in the group gets their own AI assistant.
Sounds perfect, right?
Anthropic researchers tested exactly that. In simulations.
Sharing a budget. A calendar. A group order. Everyone wants their piece.
Two setups. One AI serving the whole group.
Or one AI for every person.
Then the group grew. Four assistants? About two thirds did something.
Sixteen? One in ten.
The rest just sat out. Too little, too late.
But here's the weird part. Each assistant only knew its own person's wishes.
So it filled in the gaps.
In more than half the team runs, an assistant claimed something nobody said.
One lone assistant? About one in five.
And your request? Often, it wasn't even in the notes when the order went through.
The fixes? Naming a team lead helped with budgets. But not with bookings.
Then a rule: no checkout until messages were read... recovered many failures.
So here's the twist.
Giving everyone their own AI... made the group worse off.
Okay, last one.
Would you let an AI speak for you in a group chat? Tell me in the comments.

meta.topic: Anthropic simulation study: giving each user their own AI agent made shared decisions worse than one coordinator agent
meta.next_question: What happens when AI agents have to negotiate with each other?

facts.claim: In simulations of groups sharing a budget, calendar or group order, one coordinator AI beat a team of personal AI agents, one per user
With four agents about two thirds took action; with sixteen about one in ten (Sonnet 5)
Agents only saw their own user's notes and invented claims about others in over half of team runs (58% Opus 5) versus about one in five for a single agent
A request often was not in the booking agent's context at checkout; a designated lead helped with budgets but not bookings; blocking checkout until messages were read recovered many failures
